newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - spot business remains slow.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - spot business remains slow.

text.p: The New York physical coffee market remained sluggish this week, with few spot sales, as processors needs in the near-term were generally well met, traders said.
"Most roasters are covered into September," said one trader. "It has been very quiet."
Traders noted roastings were beginning to slow down going into the North American summer, when coffee consumption typically drops off.

Spot differentials held fairly steady this week, but quotes on many varieties were hard to come by with Central American and other quality mild beans in scarce supply ahead of the new-crop harvest in autumn.
A small amount of new-crop coffee from Brazil was beginning to make its way to market, although traders noted that recent rainfall has caused delays in harvesting.
Spot Brazilian Santos 4s were heard at some 10 cents under the July contract, while 17-18 screen Santos 2/3s fetched even-to-two cents under "C".

Spot Colombian MAMs held firm on the week at 30 cents over "C", while MAMs for July-September shipment were offered at 22 cents over September. Colombian Supremos for July shipment were quoted at 35 cents over September.
Elsewhere, Mexican coffee for spot shipment were heard at even to the board, and prime Peruvian beans for spot delivery garnered 17 cents over "C".
CSCE July coffee fell 0.35 cent a lb Friday to settle at 189.90. September ended 3.20 cents higher at 169.30.
